memory_update.text: LOPE is the cleanest US-listed direct university-services / OPM-adjacent public candidate for accredited online-degree enablement.
COUR is below the preferred USD 1B market-cap filter in the latest finance snapshot but remains an exception because it is a public modular online-degree and workforce-learning platform.
GHC provides indirect exposure through Kaplan; treat as education-services exposure inside a diversified holding company rather than a pure OPM comp.
STRA and ATGE are better classified as accredited online/workforce education operators and regulated-capacity proxies, not scarce third-party OPM suppliers.

The listed-universe chokepoint appears to be shifting away from pure legacy revenue-share OPMs toward modular platforms, internal university-services capacity, employer-funded pathways, and regulated healthcare workforce programs.

Several important node assets are not currently US-listed or are private/taken-private, including 2U, Risepoint/Academic Partnerships, Instructure/Canvas, Anthology/Blackboard, Boundless Learning, and Noodle; this limits public-market purity.

Need a follow-up pass on LMS, identity/credentialing, proctoring, student information systems, clinical placement systems, and Title IV compliance vendors; many may be private or embedded inside larger software companies.

node: Accredited online degree enablement and online program management
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the OPM and accredited online-degree enablement node. The strongest direct public exposures are not classic legacy OPM pure plays, because 2U has gone private after Chapter 11 and several large OPM assets have been sold or taken private. The investable universe therefore tilts toward modular platforms, university-services providers, accredited online operators with internal enablement capabilities, and regulated healthcare/workforce education infrastructure. Key chokepoint variables to track are revenue-share exposure, marketing/recruiting economics, compliance with Title IV and third-party-servicer rules, student-success/outcomes proof, and whether universities shift from bundled high-revenue-share models to fee-for-service or internal-capacity models.
